results.title: Submissive Homeland
results.overview: Brazil truly has the "secret sauce," and people from the outside are taking notice.  While Trump, in the United States, has his eyes on our mineral wealth, Flávio Bolsonaro—a candidate for the Brazilian presidency—is promising to hand over our rare earth elements in an attempt to win an election.  In this episode, we interview General Santos Cruz, a former minister under Jair Bolsonaro, who states: this is not what it means to be right-wing, nor is it patriotic—it is complete submission. Our minerals are strategic, both for us and for the world. The question that remains is: who will own this wealth in the years to come? Will you just sit by while it’s handed over to Trump on a silver platter?

results.title: Home Video
results.overview: A 8 year old boy playing with a camcorder, while recording his house and atmosphere he accidentally records audio of his father talking on the phone, several phone conversations of the father reveal a meticulous planning of a POGROM.  On 28 February 2002, a three-day period of inter-communal (Hindus and Muslims) violence began in the western Indian state of Gujarat. This was the first pogrom where telephones and cellphones were used as a major operational tool and the riots were meticulously per-planned, thousands of people (official number : 1,044 ) mostly Muslims were killed in the three day pogrom. The riots were particularly carried out to target Muslim.

results.title: An Akoon
results.overview: “An Akoon” means “To be”. An Akoon is a poetic, experimental, and intuitive film that confronts the weight of existence, a yearning to return to a state before becoming, before the weight of consciousness. In the depths of inner turmoil, the film dives into war, grief, anger, fear, and remorse, rooted in the profound bond between mother and child.

results.title: wedding songs
results.overview: In 16th century Shingly (Kochi, Kerala) Kabbalist Nehemiah Ben Abraham Mota was rumoured to have the power of levitation. This film assembles the ruinous remnants of the places where these and other miracles occurred.  His legacy are a series of wedding songs precariously assembled and archived, danced to by an interfaith following who worship him as a village deity.  Using celluloid processed by hand, wedding songs is a collaboration with Mota’s light and the body of the film.

results.title: Hands, trees, heads, scars
results.overview: More than 100,000 Ukrainians have already lost a limb as a result of the unjust war unleashed by Russia. Their scarred bodies are tended to by nurses behind the front lines. This is a film about touch – comforting and essential – that seeks to rekindle life from the flesh of the body where the soul is suffering.

results.title: Save the Olive Trees
results.overview: Olive trees need sunshine and, above all, water to grow if they are to bear ripe fruit. Traditional farming methods in arid Tunisia are a far cry from the romanticised image of agriculture practised in harmony with nature. They are perhaps more reminiscent of a declining sector sustained solely by the indomitable hard work of the farm labourers.

results.title: Cancer-Soul
results.overview: Hardly anyone remains untouched by the topic of cancer – whether through their own diagnosis or through a loved one. CANCER SOUL  opens a new perspective on cancer. Courageous. Holistic. And never told like this before. The film views cancer not only as a medical diagnosis, but as a complex interplay of body, mind and soul. Renowned cancer experts, doctors, alternative practitioners, energy healers and former patients speak openly about questions that concern many people:  Why does cancer develop?  What role do emotions, lifestyle, and environment play?  What treatment and support options are available – both conventional and holistic?  What can give people hope in these times?  CANCER SOUL combines modern medicine with new perspectives from naturopathy, psycho-oncology, biomedicine and spiritual approaches.  A film that doesn't pretend to have all the answers – but opens up new ways of thinking.
